content: Striae, commonly referred to as stretch marks, are irregular areas of skin that appear as bands, stripes, or lines. These marks typically develop when the skin undergoes rapid stretching, such as during periods of rapid growth, weight gain, or certain medical conditions. Symptoms of Striae Stretch marks often occur due to rapid skin stretching. They are frequently associated with the abdominal enlargement seen in pregnancy. They can also appear in children who have become rapidly obese or during the rapid growth phases of puberty in both males and females. Common locations for stretch marks include the breasts, hips, thighs, buttocks, abdomen, and flanks. Initially, stretch marks appear as parallel streaks of red, thin, glossy skin. Over time, they may fade to a whitish, scar-like appearance. These marks may be slightly depressed and have a texture that differs from normal skin. Striae can also result from abnormal collagen formation or the use of medications or chemicals that interfere with collagen production. They are sometimes associated with prolonged use of cortisone compounds, diabetes, Cushing's disease, and the postpartum period. Causes of Striae The development of striae can be attributed to several factors, including: Cushing syndrome Ehlers-Danlos syndrome Pregnancy Puberty Obesity Overuse of cortisone-containing skin creams When to Seek Urgent Medical Care If stretch marks appear without an obvious cause, such as pregnancy or rapid weight gain, it is important to contact your healthcare provider for further evaluation. Treatment Options There is no specific treatment for stretch marks. In many cases, the marks will fade or disappear once the underlying cause of skin stretching is resolved. Creams and ointments marketed to prevent stretch marks during pregnancy are generally of limited effectiveness. Preventing rapid weight gain can help reduce the likelihood of developing stretch marks related to obesity. Medical Care for Striae If you are seeking medical care for striae, consult a healthcare provider or visit a hospital that specializes in treating skin conditions. What to Expect (Outlook/Prognosis) Your healthcare provider will perform a physical examination and ask detailed questions about your symptoms, including: Is this the first time you have developed striae? When did you first notice the stretch marks? What medications have you taken? Have you used cortisone-containing skin creams? What other symptoms are you experiencing? If the striae are not caused by normal physical changes, additional tests may be conducted to determine the underlying cause.
